functional_semantics.triton: out[i] = input[N - 1 - i] into a fresh empty_like buffer, same dtype (impl_triton.py 11-15, 34).
functional_semantics.cutile: out[i] = input[N - 1 - i] into a fresh empty_like buffer, same dtype (impl_cutile.py 24-27, 35).
functional_semantics.note: Both realise the reference input.flip(0).contiguous() (impl_torch.py 5) as a materialised out-of-place reversal.

stages.triton: One kernel; each program owns a contiguous output range, loads the mirrored input addresses with a masked load (fill 0.0) and stores contiguously (impl_triton.py 11-15).
stages.cutile: One kernel; each CTA owns a contiguous output tile, reads the mirrored input indices with a per-element gather (padding value 0) and stores the tile contiguously (impl_cutile.py 24-27).
stages.note: Same single-stage reversal; the difference is only the read primitive (masked pointer load vs element gather), both reading each element once. The contract pins neither.

reduction_scan_sort.note: Pure index permutation i -> N - 1 - i.

precision.triton: No arithmetic on the data; bit-exact movement in the input dtype for fp16/bf16/fp32/int8 (impl_triton.py 14-15).
precision.cutile: No arithmetic on the data; bit-exact movement in the input dtype (impl_cutile.py 26-27).
precision.note: Same dtype in and out on both sides.

preprocessing.note: Only the output allocation on both sides.

mutation.triton: input is read-only; fresh output every call (impl_triton.py 14, 34).
mutation.cutile: input is read-only; fresh output every call (impl_cutile.py 26, 35).
mutation.note: Neither side mutates the input; the contract forbids mutation.

hardware_dispatch.note: Single code path on both sides.

fq_boundary.note: Both timed run() bodies read N elements once and write N elements once with no preprocessing traffic and nothing prepacked, exactly what bytes_expr counts (config's n is the positional N); flops_expr is a nominal one-op-per-element figure for pure data movement (config.yaml 14-15). The sweep sizes are not multiples of the tile lengths, so tail handling is exercised on both sides.
